title: Model-guard refusals name bee dispatch prepare
action: REWORK ROUND 2 — the previous round landed as commit 0d6801cd and is GOOD except for one FAIL. Do not redo it; make one focused correction on top. FAILING CHECK (goal-check judge, high confidence): `fn dispatch_kind_for_tier` at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks/model_guard.rs:560-566 maps `"review" => "reviewer"`, `"generation" => "gather"` and everything else to `"advisor"`. The extraction tier is a real, reachable case — CLAUDE_TIERS at :192 accepts `extraction` and PINNED_AGENT_TYPE at :511 maps `bee-extract` to it, so a repo whose `models.claude.extraction` is `{kind:"herding"}` or `{kind:"cli"}` (this repo IS such a repo) refuses an `Agent(bee-extract)` dispatch at :731/:748 and hands the caller `dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind advisor --json`. That invocation does NOT resolve the extraction slot: verbs/drivers/prepare.rs:627 routes `advisor` to `resolve_advisor`, and :630-636 returns `{ok:false, reason:"advisor_not_configured"}` when the advisor slot is unset; where the advisor slot IS set, prepare returns the advisor slot's payload — a different tier than the one just refused. `slot_for_kind` at prepare.rs:33-39 has no extraction arm at all, so NO --kind value resolves that slot today. The doc comment at :555-556 claiming the kind reads the same slot the guard just resolved is therefore false for extraction. FIX IT THIS WAY, and no wider: changing `bee dispatch prepare` is out of scope for this feature (docs/history/dispatch-one-door/plan.md, Out of scope) and the gap is already filed as a backlog finding. Make `dispatch_kind_for_tier` return an Option (or equivalent) that is None for any tier prepare cannot resolve, instead of falling through to `advisor`; keep `generation -> gather`, `review -> reviewer`, and `advisor -> advisor` exactly as they are. Where the tier HAS a resolving kind, the FIX text stays byte-identical to round 1. Where it does not — extraction today — the FIX must not print a `--kind` at all: instead name the transport the refused slot actually needs (the herding-exec command for a herding slot, the configured command verbatim on stdin for a cli slot, exactly as the pre-round-1 messages did) and state in one clause that `dispatch prepare` has no kind for this tier yet. Correct the now-false doc comment at :555-556 to say what the function really promises. Add a test that an `Agent(bee-extract)` dispatch under a herding-shaped extraction slot is denied with a FIX that does NOT contain the string `--kind advisor`. SECOND, SMALLER ITEM the judge flagged as a nit, fix it in the same round: the `param-on-nameless-tier` denial at :649-656 fires when a marker plus a model param meet a cli- or herding-shaped slot, and its FIX (`drop the model param (the marker alone selects the tier), or drop the marker and declare the tier whose configured model equals the param`) makes the caller reach the real door only on a second attempt. Add the resolving verb to that FIX too, using the same Option-aware helper. Everything else about the cell's original contract still holds unchanged.
